name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,446

clue.text: Mess that an angler might have had a hand in?

definitions.text: Mess that an angler might have had a hand in?

blocks.note: surface reading: a complicated tangle of trouble that someone has stirred up

blocks.clueFragment: an angler might have had a hand in
blocks.note: setter's reading: a fisherman literally puts his hand into a tin of bait

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, an angler keeps live bait in a tin and dips a hand in it; figuratively, opening one means stirring up a messy, complicated problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a situation full of unforeseen trouble, which is exactly a mess someone has created.

clue.text: Rough business heading waste disposal unit?

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
a crude, jokey description of the backside, which disposes of bodily waste

explanation.surface: A firm crudely runs off with a rubbish-disposal machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading' simply puts the first piece on top of the second in this down entry; arse is British slang for bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse and rough are synonyms describing texture or manners that are crude and unrefined.

clue.text: I'm soon dancing on E and awfully smelly

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about and swap places, so they come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; on the surface it is the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A clubber high on ecstasy is about to dance and has become rather pungent.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome describes something offensive, especially a foul and disgusting odour, so it fits an awful smell.

clue.text: Stitch up celebrity cut by Republican leader

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front
a word that is cut by another is split open with that other piece sitting in the gap

blocks.note: fame is the state of being a celebrity
the opening letter of the party name

explanation.surface: A famous figure is set up and brought down by a Republican politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To frame someone is to fabricate evidence of their guilt, which is the slang meaning of stitching them up.

clue.text: Work and work with energy on speed

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
E is the symbol for energy in physics
a rate is a speed of movement or progress

explanation.surface: Someone gets busy and puts in effort with vigour and haste.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate a machine is to work it, and of a device, to operate is to function or work.

clue.text: Teach me to fly a chopper in the jungle?

indicators.note: letters sent flying scatter and land in a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A request for lessons in piloting a helicopter over the rainforest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' and 'fly' suggest a helicopter, but the chopper is a hacking blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy knife used for hacking through dense jungle vegetation, so it is a chopping tool there.

clue.text: You could say I am good about clothes

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the word is read from its end to its start

blocks.clueFragment: You could say I am good
blocks.note: saying how good you are is boasting

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have a fine sense of what to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a slightly literary word for clothing or dress, especially of a distinctive kind.

clue.text: Ways a love goddess will inspire ecstasy

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece takes the other inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
Venus is the Roman goddess of love
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A goddess of love will move people to rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: Avenues are routes or roads, and figuratively possible methods, so both senses match ways.

clue.text: Salty bishop cut twice is full of anguish

indicators.note: cutting the word two times trims off its last two letters
being full of something means holding it inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: the word bishop with its final two letters cut away
the rack is torment, as in being on the rack

explanation.surface: A clergyman with a sharp tongue, hurt by being trimmed back, is in torment.
explanation.definitionFit: Brackish water is slightly salty, as where river water mixes with the sea.

clue.text: Hint of a strangler in Danny Dyer's face

blocks.note: a boa is a snake that kills by constriction
a trace is a slight hint or suggestion

explanation.surface: A trace of a murderer is seen on an actor's features.
explanation.walkthrough: A strangler's hint is the strangler's trace, so the snake comes first. Boat race is Cockney rhyming slang for face; Danny Dyer is an actor from East London famous for his Cockney speech.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang this boating event rhymes with face, so it is how a Londoner like that actor might say it.

clue.text: A brief dram plus Bud - that's living

indicators.note: something kept brief is cut short, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
a nip is a small drink of spirits, like a dram
bud is American slang for a friend or mate

explanation.surface: A quick whisky and a Budweiser beer make for the good life.
explanation.walkthrough: Bud looks like the beer brand, but it is a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, animate means alive or possessing life, so it can replace living.

clue.text: Nasty complaint impeding cavity? Bend over!

indicators.note: turned over means flipped so the letters of the bend run the other way
something impeding gets in the way, so it sits in the middle of the other piece

blocks.note: an arc is a curve or bend
a hole is a cavity

explanation.surface: A patient at the dentist with a painful tooth cavity is told to lean forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is a severe infectious intestinal disease, and complaint is a standard word for an illness.

clue.text: Did this, being annoyed about wife

definitions.text: Did this, being annoyed about wife

indicators.note: being about something means going around it, so one piece is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: sore is informal for angry or annoyed
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A husband cursed because his wife was getting on his nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: what someone did when cross about their wife was curse.
explanation.definitionFit: Cursing is what an irritated husband might well have done, so the whole sentence describes using bad language.

clue.text: Amazed to see One Direction having fight

blocks.note: a means one
west is a compass direction
a ruck is a scuffle or brawl

explanation.surface: A fan is stunned to see the boy band One Direction brawling.
explanation.walkthrough: One Direction is a pop group; here it splits into a number and a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Awestruck means filled with wonder or astonishment, which is a stronger synonym of amazed.

clue.text: Get out of it, perhaps with individual on Bass

indicators.note: in an across answer, a piece placed on another comes after it, so the bass abbreviation is sent first

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for bass in music
eg, for example, signals that something is perhaps one instance
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A bouncer telling an annoying single guitarist to clear off the bass.
explanation.definitionFit: Begone is an old-fashioned command to leave at once, the same as the brusque order to get out.

clue.text: Extra charge to put May in the good PM category?

definitions.text: put May in the good PM category?

blocks.note: over means in excess or extra, as in over and above
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A price hike is needed to rank Theresa May among Britain's fine Prime Ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was a British Prime Minister widely judged unsuccessful, so rating her as good would be generous.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrate is to judge something better than it is, the setter's wry verdict on ranking that leader highly.

clue.text: Slips away from area and sleeps around

indicators.note: something strewn around is scattered, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks off from a district and beds down with lots of partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes or goes by, which is what is meant by time that slips away.

clue.text: What completes Liam of Oasis: wrestling dons?

indicators.note: what completes a word is its closing letter, the one that finishes it off
wrestling bodies twist and grapple, so the letters get tangled into a new order

blocks.note: the final letter of the name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about what finishes off the Oasis singer Liam Gallagher, with wrestling teachers in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Dons look like university lecturers but are Mafia bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: Mafia members are called mafiosi or mafiosos, and their bosses are known as dons.

clue.text: Time Her Maj should enter a service sober

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so these pieces are placed within the other

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
a, plus use, which is service as in being of service

explanation.surface: It is time for the Queen to attend a solemn church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Her Maj is a jokey British short form of Her Majesty, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severe and plain, without indulgence, which matches the serious, plain sense of sober.

clue.text: German building kitsch, loss-making houses

indicators.note: the run of words houses the answer, holding it inside across the gap between them

blocks.note: letters running from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: Tacky German construction firms that lose money.
explanation.definitionFit: Schloss is the German word for a castle or palace, so it is a building in Germany.

clue.text: Intense, but unopened message about Hoskins

indicators.note: a thing unopened has not had its front broken into, so its first letter goes

blocks.note: a text is a phone message
re means concerning or about
the setter names himself, so his name stands for me

explanation.surface: A heated text that nobody opened, concerning the setter himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoskins is this puzzle's setter, so the name stands for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme describes something of the highest degree, as does intense when used of feelings or heat.

clue.text: Incidents in the 100 and 200 metres?

blocks.note: first meaning: things that happen, occurrences
second meaning: races on an athletics programme

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests incidents happening during sprint races; the two parts are separate meanings, the second an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurrences are happenings, and individual races at a sports meeting are its competitive contests, each called by this word.

clue.text: Stop, you ruddy bore

blocks.note: to end is to stop
U is text-speak for you
ruddy means reddish

explanation.surface: An exasperated plea to a tedious person to shut up.
explanation.walkthrough: Bore looks like a noun insulting someone, but it is the past tense of bear; ruddy is also a mild British swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: To have borne hardship is to have put up with or tolerated it, the past sense of suffering through.

clue.text: Are they a bit higher than belly laughs?

definitions.text: Are they a bit higher than belly laughs?

blocks.clueFragment: a bit higher than belly laughs
blocks.note: surface reading: lighter, higher-pitched laughs than deep guffaws
setter's reading: the word starts with a slang term for breasts, which sit just above the belly

explanation.walkthrough: Small nervous giggles are pitched higher than hearty belly laughs, and the first part of the answer is also crude slang for a body part above the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Short suppressed giggles are lighter and higher in tone than full hearty laughs from the stomach.

clue.text: So lacking in love, my editor bought drugs

indicators.note: lacking love means without the zero-shaped letter that stands for love in tennis

blocks.note: the word so without its O
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
ed is short for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor with no love left bought illegal substances.
explanation.walkthrough: My is an exclamation here, not a possessive; love is O, as in a tennis score of nil.
explanation.definitionFit: To score is slang for obtaining illegal drugs, so it can replace bought drugs.

clue.text: I'd neither gone off or was left

indicators.note: food that has gone off is spoiled, so these letters are spoilt into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone says they neither went away nor stayed behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' suggests departing, but here it is being left something in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who inherited property was left it in a will, so the passive phrase means the same.

clue.text: In flagrante, but half-upset (cold room)

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, and only half of the phrase is overturned to run the other way

blocks.note: caught in flagrante, in the act, is caught at it
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Lovers caught in the act are somewhat flustered in a chilly bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: In flagrante delicto is Latin for caught red-handed, often meaning caught having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is a room in the roof space at the top of a house.

clue.text: Summer days in embrace of a European Romeo

indicators.note: to be in someone's embrace is to be held within their arms, so these letters sit inside

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for day, doubled for the plural
E is the abbreviation for European
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Summer holidays spent in the arms of a Continental lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Summer is not the season but someone who sums, adding figures up.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as one who sums, a summer is a person or machine that totals figures, exactly what this word means.

clue.text: Half-pint of cider taken regularly after whisky?

indicators.note: taking something at regular intervals means picking every second letter

blocks.note: a short is a measure of spirits such as whisky, hence the question mark for an example
the second and fourth letters of the drink

explanation.surface: A pub drinker regularly has half a pint of cider following a whisky chaser.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-pint looks like a beer measure but is slang for a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-pint is informal for a very small person, and a shortie is likewise a short person.

clue.text: Beast always chasing after flushed duke

blocks.note: a flushed face is red
D is the abbreviation for duke
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: An animal forever pursuing a blushing aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: This large deer is a wild animal of British forests and moors, and beast is a general word for an animal.

clue.text: Having changed top, bother to work out?

indicators.note: changing the top of a word means swapping its first letter for another

blocks.note: fuss is trouble or bother

explanation.surface: Someone who has had a new top fitted asks if it is worth going to the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter replaces the F; the definition supplies it. Work out looks like exercising, but it means figure out.
explanation.definitionFit: To suss something is British slang for realising or figuring it out, so it means work out.

clue.text: Cook did entrées, then pounded the meat?

indicators.note: to cook is to mix things up and alter them, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chef prepares the main courses, having beaten the steak flat first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the chef's role in the kitchen, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat is tenderised by beating it with a mallet to break down tough fibres, so it has been pounded.
